question: What's the best solar generator for power outages?
query: best solar generators portable power stations for home power outages 2026 reviews capacity expandable solar charging

replays.text:
**Best overall for home power outages: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.** It has a 4,096Wh capacity and 4,000W output, can take up to 2,600W of solar input, and can expand to 48kWh—making it the strongest choice here for running more essentials or preparing for longer outages. It also supports an optional transfer-switch kit for powering selected home circuits. ([OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

If you want something easier to move, consider the **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: it has 2,042Wh capacity, weighs 39 lb, and supports solar recharging. ([OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

One caveat: even a large portable power station may not keep major appliances running for days. Check both **capacity (Wh)** and **output (W)** against what you plan to power; solar recharge also depends on sunlight and can be slow. ([Consumer Reports](https://www.consumerreports.org/home-garden/generators/best-portable-power-stations-a4748703075/))

**Best for serious home-outage backup: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3.** It has a 4,096 Wh battery and 4,000 W output, can accept up to 2,600 W of solar input, and can expand to 48 kWh. It’s also compatible with an optional transfer-switch kit for powering essential home circuits. That combination makes it a stronger choice for outages than a small, easy-to-carry power station. ([PowerOutage.us](https://poweroutage.us/generators/best-solar-portable-generators); [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

If you want something more portable, the **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is a lighter alternative at 39 lb, with 2,042 Wh capacity and solar-panel support. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

One caveat: even a large battery station may run out during a long outage. These are best for keeping selected essentials going; how long depends on what you plug in. ([Consumer Reports](https://www.consumerreports.org/home-garden/generators/best-portable-power-stations-a4748703075/))

**Best for serious outage backup: [EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station).** It combines **4,096 Wh of capacity** with **4,000 W output**, supports up to **2,600 W of solar input**, and can expand to **48 kWh**. That makes it the strongest pick here if you want to run more than phones and lights—or build toward backup for essential home circuits. It’s a substantial, costly unit, though.

If you want something more portable, the **[Jackery Explorer 2000 v2](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)** has 2,042 Wh capacity and weighs 39 lb, according to Outdoor Gear Lab. For a smaller budget and lighter needs, Good Housekeeping names the **[EcoFlow RIVER 3](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/home-products/g70424851/top-tested-solar-powered-generators/)** its best-value pick.

One caveat: solar generators are best for **short outages and essential loads**, not automatically for powering an entire home for days. Solar recharging can be slow, especially in cloudy weather, so choose capacity based on what you need to run and for how long. ([Consumer Reports](https://www.consumerreports.org/home-garden/generators/best-portable-power-stations-a4748703075/))
